reviews.rationale: Colored sleeve, white lining and doubled inner-to-outer return can be realized on the kaftan wrist without altering face/hair. Complete alternative LINING01 makes the paper-holding hand clearer, but the cuff transition competes with the petition contact at the same small area; DIRECT15 spreads its signal over the front cloth and preserves hand simplicity.

The full garment-tie/top-clasp/cord/knot/ornament/tassel chain is feasible only as a deliberate additional hanging accessory in this unbound costume. It adds another dangling route beside the paper cord and would shift the Ottoman-inspired textile hierarchy toward a distinct Korean accessory; no requester lock forbids it, but this creativity1 scene gains less expressive value than the local kaftan motif.

The complete dark round-collared robe with flat square patch, four edges and two cranes would replace the kaftan front with a different court costume system. This is not generic gold decoration or proof of actual rank; the bounded image test chooses the close Ottoman textile alternative instead.

The shoe requires the sole-to-central-wood support connection, toe and heel overhang and ground support together. The seated tabletop moment conceals footwear; showing them demands a lower full-body frame and shifts attention from reference face and handover. NOT_COVERED in this arm.

The rear-only sleeve join, open underarm and cuff-cord path form a kariginu structure, not an ordinary broad sleeve. The current kaftan and table-supported arm cannot show the rear attachment and open axilla together without changing garment construction, arm elevation and view. NOT_COVERED here.

A single flat shaku must stand upright in one hand with lower-end finger contact. Its full court gesture would occupy the hand kept relaxed beside the petition and compete with the unfinished transfer; neither a paper nor closed fan qualifies. This is a distinct prop/action requiring a new whole alternative, less close than DIRECT15.

The fitted polonaise bodice, three separate rear puffs and visible separate petticoat require a rear-or-side garment view. The face-and-table layout does not show those regions together, and a three-puff silhouette cannot prove hidden gathering rings or cords. NOT_COVERED here.

The mantua needs connected bodice-to-rear train, separate broad petticoat and triangular front stomacher together. It would replace the kaftan and demand front/back/train legibility beyond the intimate tabletop composition. It is not compatible as a single triangular decoration. NOT_COVERED.

The opened pomander needs central stem, multiple hollow hinged segments, sliding covers and upper loop-cap visible together. It could stand on the table, but would introduce a second intricate tabletop apparatus beside the paper and cord. A perforated pendant is insufficient; aroma and efficacy stay unobservable. NOT_COVERED.

The band joining upper purple settings and lower comb teeth must be visible. Wearing it in the short reference bob would hide teeth; laying it on the table would add a detached still-life object without strengthening the handover. It cannot prove a complete matched parure, mineral identity or gold purity. NOT_COVERED.

The closed box requires separate lid seam, body and chased floral relief across lid and sides, with credible support scale. A small gift-box inference adds contents or motive not visible; placing it beside the petition divides the simple handover narrative. NOT_COVERED.

The angular peaked fabric hood frames forehead and face but would cover the crown and much of the requested short bob. It is a distinct gable outline, not a round French hood, and cannot show hidden brass frame. The reference hair duty makes this a poor option; NOT_COVERED.

The complete braid-edge/tassel-head/free-strands route is realized in TRIM13. It gives tactile continuity but creates another dangling line near the loose petition cord and small hand details; DIRECT15 gives a broad flat pattern while keeping the interrupted transfer visually simpler.

REFORM14 realizes fez, frock coat and separate fitted trousers on the same woman, retaining visible bob/bangs and reference face. The full-length view is needed for all three garments and shifts the emotional distance and period reading; no actual rank or wearer history is inferred. The closer kaftan scene gives stronger reference presence at creativity1.

DIRECT15 replaces the authorial teal kaftan with magenta and repeated triangular triads of three yellow circles on the robe fabric. It preserves every source component/count and representation layer without importing wave bands, jeweled buttons, norigae, rank or identity. The broad motif can remain visible with the woman, paper and messenger together. This is direct postcore source-informed testing, not natural retrieval exposure or native approval.

Twisted hemp circles a plain mourning garment, with a secured front knot and tied ends. It would require a deliberate mourning-costume narrative that the current court pause does not establish, and a still cannot prove death, kinship or grade. NOT_COVERED, not a prohibited source.

The pale inner shitagasane must emerge below the outer sokutai back and form a continuous floor-supported rear train. Current frontal seated/table framing cannot show emergence and rear path; it cannot be substituted by a shoulder cape or pale front skirt. NOT_COVERED.

The doubled dark headcloth must cover forehead/crown and drape over rear shoulders, with folded edge beside face. This conceals the reference bangs and short bob and would require a changed reference-use duty. No hidden paper or occupation inferred; NOT_COVERED.
Badge motifs varied historically; a generated pair of cranes does not verify a real office or rank. Diagnostic is not positive imagery, native approval or an automatic hard gate.
A covered hood profile cannot prove concealed brass wire; inspect an exposed construction view separately. Diagnostic is not positive imagery, native approval or an automatic hard gate.
Three puffs do not show whether inner rings, cords, ribbons or outer buttons produced them. Diagnostic is not positive imagery, native approval or an automatic hard gate.
Visible compartments do not prove aroma, contents or disease prevention. Diagnostic is not positive imagery, native approval or an automatic hard gate.
A comb is one object; matched jewelry requires the requested separate pieces and correspondence to be visible. Diagnostic is not positive imagery, native approval or an automatic hard gate.
A still posture cannot demonstrate a curtsy followed by stepping aside and backing away. Diagnostic is not positive imagery, native approval or an automatic hard gate.

R2V15.required: Each yellow motif has exactly three circular discs in triangular arrangement; at least two complete repeats are visible together.
Multiple complete clusters repeat across the same magenta kaftan body.
The yellow clusters lie on and follow the robe fabric plane, with a visible textile carrier.
Discs are readable as flat robe-surface motifs, distinct from buttons or hanging ornaments.

pixel_policy: Every component/count/carrier/relation together; partial or unobservable is fail; native_approval remains false; requester acceptance pending.
